item.title: The maximum area of a snake polyomino in a $12 \times n$ rectangle
item.description: arXiv:2611.26640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A snake polyomino is a set of cells of the square lattice whose cells, under edge adjacency, induce a path. Let $T(m,n)$ be the largest number of cells of a snake polyomino contained in an $m \times n$ rectangle, equivalently the largest number of vertices of an induced path in the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$ (OEIS A360917). Blondin Mass\'e and Goupil determined $T(m,n)$ for all $m \le 5$ and proposed the general case as a conjecture; for $m = 12$, entry A397153 of the OEIS records a conjectured generating function, contributed by Goupil in July 2026, which has remained unproved. We prove it. For every $n \ge 1$ other than $n \in \{2,3,\dots,10,12\}$ one has $T(12,n) = 44k + c_r$ where $n = 6k+r$ with $0 \le r < 6$ and $(c_0,\dots,c_5) = (5,12,19,27,34,42)$, and the ten remaining values are $18,26,33,40,47,55,62,70,77$ and $92$. The proof has two independent halves. The upper bound comes from a column-profile transfer system read in the max-plus semiring: a single entrywise inequality $v_{46} \le 44 + v_{40}$ between two value vectors on its useful core propagates to all larger indices because the max-plus action is monotone and additively homogeneous. The lower bound comes from explicit periodic snakes, one for each residue class, which are checked against the definition of a snake and not against the transfer system. The same method settles every height up to $12$; heights $6$ through $11$ had no formula in the literature, and we record them as well.
item.dc:creator: Tong Niu

item.title: Extremal Ky Fan $p$-$k$ norms of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.26648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a two-parameter extension of Nikiforov's extremal problems for graph norms, focusing on the quantity $$ S_{p,k}(G) = \left(\sum_{i=1}^{k}\sigma_i(G)^p\right)^{1/p}, $$ where $p\ge1$, and $\sigma_1(G) \ge \cdots \ge \sigma_n(G)$ are the singular values of the adjacency matrix of an $n$-vertex graph $G$. This quantity provides a common generalization of the Ky Fan $k$-norm and the Schatten $p$-norm, which correspond to the cases $p=1$ and $k=n$, respectively. We establish upper and lower bounds and characterize extremal and near-extremal graphs within specified parameter ranges. For each fixed $k \ge 4$, we determine an explicit exponent $\vartheta_k \in [1,2)$ such that the balanced complete $k$-partite graph is the unique maximizer for all sufficiently large orders, and we characterize the unique graph attaining the second-largest value. In particular, this determines the maximum Ky Fan $4$-norm for all sufficiently large orders. At these exponents, any maximizer with a fixed edge deficit from the Tur\'{a}n graph's edge count belongs to an explicit finite family of complete $k$-partite graphs (whenever such a realization exists), whereas a fixed edge surplus is uniquely maximized by adding a star inside a largest part of the balanced graph. Furthermore, we quantify the relation between small absolute norm deficits and graph structure, demonstrating that relative near-optimality alone does not guarantee structural proximity. We also obtain a vertex-partition lower bound featuring an optimal universal remainder coefficient and complete equality conditions. These results provide structural answers to Nikiforov's norm questions in the two-parameter setting, linking extremal values to uniqueness, prescribed edge counts, and the structure of near-extremal graphs.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Lin

item.title: The Manhattan cospectrality of the cocktail party graph
item.description: arXiv:2611.26650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$ of order $N$ with adjacency eigenvalues $\lambda_{1}(G)\geq \cdots\geq\lambda_{N}(G),$ the cospectrality of $G$ is the smallest value of $\sum_{i}\left\vert \lambda_{i}(G)-\lambda_{i}(H)\right\vert $ over all graphs $H$ of order $N$ not isomorphic to $G.$ Abdollahi and Zakeri (Ars Math. Contemp. 22(1) (2022) P1.06) conjectured that the cospectrality of the cocktail party graph $CP_{n}$ is attained exactly at the graph $H_{n}.$ This graph is obtained from $K_{1,2,\ldots,2}$ by attaching a pendant vertex to the vertex of the part of size one. We prove this conjecture for every $n\geq2$ by showing that only three explicit graphs (two for $n=2$) are at distance less than $2$ from $CP_{n}.$ We work with the complement of a competing graph. First we remove its components $K_{2}.$ Then we treat the case in which its main component has a dominating vertex. The remaining cases are reduced to finitely many small graphs. The proof is computer-assisted, and all computations concern explicit finite lists of graphs.
item.dc:creator: Irena M. Jovanovi\'c, Jelena Sedlar, Riste \v{S}krekovski

item.title: Detour different-distance sets in graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.26653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The detour distance $D(u,v)$ between two vertices of a connected graph is the length of a longest $u,v$-path. A set $S$ of vertices is a detour different-distance set if no vertex outside $S$ has the same detour distance to two vertices of $S$. We study the lower and upper detour different-distance numbers $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)$ and $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)$, the smallest and largest orders of maximal such sets; this is the detour analogue of the different-distance sets of Hedetniemi, Hedetniemi, Laskar and Mulder. The two notions coincide on trees, cycles, complete bipartite graphs and the Petersen graph, but differ in general: for instance, detour different-distance sets may contain triangles or induce $4$-cycles. We determine both numbers for many families, among them wheels, fans, windmills, hypercubes, helms, flowers, books, ladders, prisms, M\"obius ladders, crowns, gears, Dutch windmills and complete multipartite graphs, and for joins, coronas and lexicographic products. We prove that $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)$ is at most the detour diameter; that $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)=n-1$ if and only if $G$ is a path; that $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)=\mathrm{DD}_D(G)=1$ whenever two vertices are joined by Hamiltonian paths to all other vertices; that $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)=\mathrm{DD}_D(G)=2$ for Hamiltonian-laceable graphs and, more generally, for bipartite graphs in which each part contains two vertices whose detour distances to the other part are constant; and that $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ for Hamiltonian graphs.
item.dc:creator: Ammar Alsinai, Hanan Ahmed

item.title: M\"obius expansion and pointwise energy transfer over arbitrary fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.26661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a field of positive characteristic $p$, and let $A\subset F^\times$ have $N$ elements. We prove that, for every $\lambda\in F^\times$, \[ \card{A+\lambda A^{-1}}\gg\min\{N^{10/9},(pN^2)^{1/3}\}. \] This improves the exponent $31/30$ to $10/9$ in the common small-set range. Over prime fields the bound strengthens to $\min\{N^{10/9},(pN)^{1/2}\}$. Analogous bounds hold for $Af(A)$ when $f$ is a M\"obius transformation satisfying the stated nondegeneracy conditions. In characteristic zero, the bound $N^{10/9}$ remains valid. No subfield-avoidance condition is required.
item.dc:creator: Yao Zhi

item.title: On the number of edge-disjoint $K_r$ in $K_{r+1}$-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.26669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gy\H ori and Keszegh [\emph{Combinatorica} \textbf{37} (2017), 1113--1124] proved that every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint triangles. We extend this result to cliques of arbitrary fixed order. Specifically, we prove that for every fixed integer $r\ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every $K_{r+1}$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $t_{r-1}(n)+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint copies of $K_r$, where $t_{r-1}(n)$ denotes the number of edges in the Tur\'an graph $T_{r-1}(n)$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $G$ is obtained from $T_{r-1}(n)$ by adding edges within one of its parts, with the added edges forming a triangle-free graph.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Liu, Qinghou Zeng

item.title: Partial sums of Rogers-Ramanujan functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.26719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Explicit positive multisums on base q^5 for the Rogers-Ramanujan sum function and its partial sum are given. 32 combinatorial interpretations for these identities are given. The classical mod 5 Rogers-Ramanujan identities are recovered as a limiting case. These results are equivalent to a quintic basic hypergeometric identity.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Stanton

item.title: Connected Cayley Approximation of Power Graphs of Finite Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.26732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a nontrivial finite group \(G\), we define its connected intersection density as the maximum, over all connected Cayley graphs on \(G\), of the proportion of edges that also belong to the undirected power graph of \(G\). We show that this density is \(1\) if and only if \(G\) is cyclic, and that it is \(1/4\), \(1/6\), and \(1/12\) for \(A_4\), \(S_4\), and \(A_5\), respectively. For the dihedral group of order \(2n\), with \(n\geq 3\), we give a general formula and show that the connected intersection density equals \((\binom{n}{2}+1)/n^2\) if and only if \(n\) is a prime power. We also give a formula for the connected intersection density of dicyclic groups. For generalized quaternion groups of order \(2N\), where \(N=2^{m-1}\geq 4\), the density is \(\frac{N^2+8}{2N(N+1)}\). For the elementary abelian group \(C_p^r\), where \(p\) is prime and \(r\geq 1\), the density is \(p^{1-r}\).
item.dc:creator: Zahra Rabie, Mohammad A. Iranmanesh

item.title: Generalized anti-Ramsey numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.26748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The anti-Ramsey number was introduced by Erd\H{o}s, Simonovits, and S\'os and is defined to be the maximum number of colors that can be used to color the edges of a graph to avoid a rainbow copy of some graph. One can generalize this by, instead of forbidding a rainbow copy of a graph, putting a cap on the number of colors that appear on any copy of that graph. To be precise, let $\AR(G,H,q)$ be the maximum number of colors that can be used to color $E(G)$ so that every copy of $H$ sees at most $q$ colors. One can see that $\AR(G,H,q)$ is nondecreasing in $q$. In this paper, we investigate the linear and quadratic thresholds of $\AR(G,H,q)$ when $G=K_n$ and $H$ is connected.
item.dc:creator: Deepak Bal, Jonathan Cutler

item.title: Avoiding squares over words with lists of size three
item.description: arXiv:2611.26768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every sequence of lists of size three admits an infinite square-free word, establishing that the Thue choice number of the path is three. More precisely, the number of compatible square-free words of length $n$ is at least $c(5/4)^n$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. The proof combines a computer-assisted construction of weights with the weighted counting method previously introduced by the author. We first consider words avoiding only squares of bounded period and use a finite state model to certify a uniform lower bound on their growth. The counting argument then controls the loss caused by excluding longer squares. The main new ingredient is a coarser description of the states, which makes the computation feasible without restricting the union of the lists. The same computation yields a deterministic polynomial-time strategy for constructing an infinite square-free word when each list is chosen adversarially after the preceding letters have been fixed.
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Rosenfeld

item.title: Isolation in Random Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.26781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study isolation in the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$. When $p=o(1)$ and $np\to\infty$, allowing an $F$-free graph on the undominated vertices gives the same first-order asymptotics for every fixed forest $F$ as the domination number $\gamma(G)$ in $G(n,p)$. For the ordinary isolation number $\iota(G)$ ($F$ is an edge) we prove two-point concentration when $p$ is bounded away from $1$ and $np^2/(\log n)^3\to\infty$. We also identify a transition in the gap $\gamma(G)-\iota(G)$ when $\log(1/p)=o(\log n)$. This gap tends to infinity in probability when $p$ is well below $(\log\log n/\log n)^2$ and is at most one with high probability when $p$ is well above this scale. Finally, for every fixed graph $F$, we show that the classical minimum degree bound for domination is asymptotically sharp for $F$-isolation, even for regular host graphs.
item.dc:creator: Laurentiu Ploscaru

item.title: Compression with wildcards: The maximum anticliques of K\"onig-Egarv\'ary graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.26786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By definition a K\"onig-Egarv\'ary graph is such that the cardinality of each maximum matching equals the cardinality of each minimum vertex-cover. Each bipartite graph has this property. We unravel the structure of the family MACL(G) of all maximum anticliques (independent sets) of a K\"onig-Egarv\'ary graph G. This enables us to enumerate $MACL(G)$ not only in output polynomial time, but also in a compressed format (using wildcards). All of this can be viewed as an instance where ALL minimum solutions of a submodular function can be enumerated efficiently.
item.dc:creator: Marcel Wild

item.title: Polynomial sequences of Simplex pivots on 0/1-polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.26830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the number of Simplex pivots needed to solve linear programs over $0/1$-polytopes, starting from an arbitrary feasible basis and counting degenerate pivots. It has been known since the 1990s that from any extreme point of a 0/1-polytope there exists a monotone path of linear length to an optimal one. However, translating this into a polynomial sequence of Simplex pivots, i.e., improving basis exchanges, has remained an open question. We here provide an affirmative answer, showing that for every 0/1-polytope $\mathcal P \subseteq \mathbb R^d$, an optimal basis can be reached with $O(d^3)$ Simplex pivots, independently of the number of inequalities and of the size of the coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Laura Sanit\`a

item.title: Large 4-tangles in matroids are characterized by large internally 4-connected minors
item.description: arXiv:2611.26846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tangles were first introduced by Robertson and Seymour as an abstract way of treating highly connected substructures in graphs and matroids. For any truly highly connected substructure in a graph or matroid, all of the low-order separations in the object can be oriented towards it. This gives rise to a tangle. A standard question is whether every tangle of a given order in fact arises from some concrete highly connected substructure, such as a minor. It is well known that tangles of order two and three (in both graphs and matroids) are characterized by maximal $2$-connected and $3$-connected minors, respectively. For tangles of order four, it is necessary to consider a weaker notion of connectivity. Carmesin and Kurkofka showed that, for graphs, internal $4$-connectedness suffices. For matroids, Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple and Whittle showed that $4$-tangles arise from weakly $4$-connected minors, that is, minors in which every $3$-separation has a side with at most four elements. In the latter case, the breadth of the tangle (a measure of its complexity) can be preserved exactly, but the authors also asked whether a stronger notion of $4$-connectivity could be used while preserving some fraction of the breadth. In this paper, we answer this question in the affirmative by showing that, in a matroid, any $4$-tangle of sufficiently large breadth is determined by an internally $4$-connected minor whose unique $4$-tangle also has large breadth.
item.dc:creator: Nick Brettell, Johannes Carmesin, Tony Huynh, Matthew E. Kroeker, Florian Lehner, Geoff Whittle

item.title: Small spherical 7-designs in prime dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.26879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every prime $p\ge 29$, we construct an antipodal spherical $7$-design on $S^{p-1}$ with $42(p-1)(p+2)^2$ points. The construction uses eigenlines of finite Weil operators.
item.dc:creator: Andriy Bondarenko, Dmytro Mitin

item.title: Structure of linear extensions of posets and lexicographic shelling
item.description: arXiv:2611.26888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study some structure of linear extensions of a finite poset $P$ by investigating partial orders on the maximal chains of the lattice of order ideals $J(P)$. These partial orders on the maximal chains of $J(P)$ are called maximal chain descent orders (MCDO). MCDOs come from EL-labelings of finite bounded posets and encode the structure of shellings arising from EL-labelings. Every linear extension of $P$ gives an EL-labeling of $J(P)$, and so generates an MCDO. Our main question is: when do different linear extensions of $P$ result in isomorphic MCDOs? We give partial answers to this question. In particular, we prove that linear extensions that are related by an automorphism of $P$ result in isomorphic MCDOs. Additionally, we show that for a certain family of posets, a linear extension $l$ and Sch\"utzenberger's evacuation of $l$ generate isomorphic MCDOs. In this case, the isomorphism comes from a well known isomorphism of the weak order on permutations.
item.dc:creator: Clarice Andorno, Stephen Lacina

item.title: On the cyclic and dihedral Ramsey numbers of separated caterpillars and nested matchings
item.description: arXiv:2611.26896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider all graphs to have vertex sets of the form $\{0, 1, 2, \ldots, n-1\}$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$. For graphs $H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k$, the cyclic Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{cyc}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ is the smallest $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every $k$-edge-coloring of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H_j$ in color $j$ for some $j \in \{1, 2, \ldots, k\}$, with the vertices appearing in the same cyclic order as in $H_j$. The dihedral Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{dih}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ is defined analogously, with the difference that the direction of the cyclic order is ignored. For $n \ge 2$, a separated caterpillar of order $n$ is a graph obtained by a cyclic shift of the vertex labels from a tree of order $n$ whose edges can be written as $u_1 v_1, u_2 v_2, \ldots, u_{n-1} v_{n-1}$ so that $u_1 \leq u_2 \le \cdots \le u_{n-1} < v_{n-1} \le \cdots \le v_2 \le v_1$, while the trivial graph $K_1$ is the separated caterpillar of order one. For even $n \ge 2$, the nested matching of order $n$ is the $1$-regular graph in which each vertex $v$ is adjacent to $n - 1 - v$. We prove that if $H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k$ are separated caterpillars, then $R_{\mathrm{cyc}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ and $R_{\mathrm{dih}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ are both equal to the Ramsey number of stars of the same orders, which was determined by Burr and Roberts. We also prove that $R_{\mathrm{cyc}}(F, H) = R_{\mathrm{dih}}(F, H) = 1 + (a-1)(b-1)$ for any graph $F$ of order $a \ge 2$ in which each vertex $v$ is adjacent to $(v + 1) \bmod a$ and any separated caterpillar $H$ of order $b \in \mathbb{N}$. Moreover, we determine the multicolor cyclic Ramsey numbers whose arguments are stars and nested matchings, provided that at most one of these nested matchings has order divisible by four. Some special cases of these results were recently obtained by Kucheriya, Petr and Yan.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Damnjanovi\'c, Daniil Furmanov, Jon A. Maccarello, Julien Menet

item.title: An Infinite Family of Overpartition Congruences Modulo 1944
item.description: arXiv:2611.26943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\overline p(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$. We prove that $\overline p(16^\alpha(96n+76))\equiv0\pmod{1944}$ for all nonnegative integers $\alpha$ and $n$, extending the congruence for $\overline p(96n+76)$ established by Smoot. The key step is a three-term congruence modulo $243$ relating $\overline p(m)$, $\overline p(16m)$, and $\overline p(256m)$ for $m\equiv4\pmod6$. We derive this relation and the two initial congruences using theta-function dissections. A separate theta-series argument establishes divisibility by $8$.
item.dc:creator: Li Zhang

item.title: Counterexamples to a conjecture of Gao and Gu on weighted Catalan numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.26953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct infinitely many counterexamples to a conjecture of Gao and Gu on when the 2-adic valuations of weighted Catalan numbers equal those of Catalan numbers.
item.dc:creator: Ryota Inagaki, Dimana Pramatarova

item.title: Stability of independence polynomials of well-covered Ferrers graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.26962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every root of the independence polynomial of a well-covered Ferrers graph lies in the open unit disk centered at $-1$, that is, $|x+1|<1$. Consequently, the polynomial is strictly stable. We also exhibit a general Ferrers graph whose independence polynomial is not stable.
item.dc:creator: Ta Quang Anh, Do Trong Hoang, Nguyen Minh Nhat

item.title: The Order of the Inertia Bound for Random Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.27000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an $n$-vertex graph $G$, let $n_{\geq0}(G)$ be the minimum number of nonnegative eigenvalues among zero-diagonal Hermitian matrices supported on $G$, allowing zero edge weights. For $n\geq2$ and $G\sim G(n,1/2)$, we prove $n_{\geq0}(G)\geq c_2n/\log(2n)$ with probability at least $1-\exp(-c_1n\log(2n))$, where $c_1,c_2>0$ are absolute constants. This proves a Hermitian extension of the Kwan--Wigderson conjecture. With high probability, $n_{\geq0}(G)=\Theta(n/\log n)$ and $n_{\geq0} G)/\alpha(G)=\Theta(n/(\log n)^2)$, where $\alpha(G)$ is the independence number. Using Alon's constructions, we obtain, for every sufficiently large $n$, a $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)=2$ and $n_{\geq0}(G)=\Omega(n^{1/3})$. For infinitely many $n$, we also obtain $n$-vertex graphs $H$ with Shannon capacity $3$ and $n_{\geq0}(H)=\Omega(n^{1/4})$.
item.dc:creator: Zhengbo Chen, Xiao-Dong Zhang

item.title: Nowhere-zero $9$-flows of signed graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.27023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1983, Bouchet conjectured that every flow-admissible signed graph admits a nowhere-zero $6$-flow. DeVos et al.\ proved that every flow-admissible signed graph admits a nowhere-zero $11$-flow. In this paper, we show that every flow-admissible signed graph admits a nowhere-zero $9$-flow.
item.dc:creator: Miaomiao Han, Jiaao Li, Rong Luo, Xiangqian Zhou

item.title: Independence number, clique number, and maximum degree
item.description: arXiv:2611.27126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every integer $r \ge 3$, every $K_r$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with minimum degree $\delta(G) > (5r-11)n/(5r-5)$ satisfies $\alpha(G) \ge n/(r-1)$. This resolves a conjecture posed by Brandt in 2001 and establishes the sharp minimum-degree threshold for guaranteeing an independent set of size at least $n/(r - 1)$ in $K_r$-free graphs.
item.dc:creator: Xinmin Hou, Xiangyang Wang

item.title: Radio antipodal number for the Cartesian product of a complete graph and a path
item.description: arXiv:2611.27184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A radio antipodal labeling of a graph $G$ is a function $f$ that assigns a non negative integer to each vertex in such a way that for any pair of distinct vertices $x$ and $y$, the condition $|f(x)-f(y)| \geq d-d(x,y)$ is satisfied, where $d$ and $d(x,y)$ represent the diameter of graph $G$, and distance between $x$ and $y$ in graph $G$, respectively. The span of radio antipodal labeling $f$ is defined as $span(f) = \max\{|f(x)-f(y)| : x,y \in V(G)\}$. The radio antipodal number of graph $G$, denoted by $an(G)$, is defined as $an(G) := \min_{f}\{span(f)\}$ with minimum taken over all radio antipodal labelings $f$ of $G$. A radio antipodal labeling $f$ of $G$ is optimal if $span(f) = an(G)$. In this paper, we give the exact radio antipodal number of the Cartesian product of a complete graph and a path.
item.dc:creator: Payal Vasoya, Devsi Bantva

item.title: Tight Probabilistic Aspects of Friends-and-Strangers Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.27207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Friends-and-strangers graphs, introduced by Defant and Kravitz, model arrangements of people on positions. We consider two graphs $X$ and $Y$ on $n$ vertices. The vertices of $X$ represent positions with edges denoting adjacencies while the vertices of $Y$ represent people with edges denoting friendships. Their \emph{friends-and-strangers graph} is denoted by $\mathsf{FS}(X,Y)$. Its vertices are all one-to-one placements of people on positions, and two placements are adjacent if one can swap two friends on adjacent positions to get from one placement to the other. A fundamental question is whether or not a friends-and-strangers graph is connected. A natural probabilistic analog is ``If $X$ and $Y$ are independently sampled Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi graphs with $n$ vertices and edge probability $p,$ what is the threshold probability for $\mathsf{FS}(X,Y)$ to be connected with high probability?'' Alon, Defant, and Kravitz (2023) showed that $p = n^{-1/2+o(1)}$ is the threshold probability and conjectured that $p = \Theta(n^{-1/2}).$ Milojevi\'{c} (2024) disproved this by showing $p = \Omega(n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log n})$ is necessary for connectivity with high probability. In this work, we prove a matching upper bound, thus establishing that the threshold is $p = \Theta(n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log n}).$
item.dc:creator: Neil Krishnan

item.title: On the Delandtsheer Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.27275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Delandtsheer Conjecture of 1988 that a line-primitive automorphism group of a finite linear space is point-primitive.
item.dc:creator: Zhilin Zhang, Shenglin Zhou

item.title: The Four-Cycle Extremal Number of the Seven-Cube
item.description: arXiv:2611.27284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the largest number of edges in a four-cycle-free subgraph of the seven-dimensional hypercube is 304. In a hypothetical 305-edge subgraph, three-star counting and a local computational lemma force every degree to be four or five. A square-counting identity and an inequality for opposite facets then reduce the proof to five candidate facet profiles, excluded by two further local statements. The three computational statements concern only six-dimensional cubes and are certified by 21 propositional refutations.
item.dc:creator: Zheli Zhou, Haitong Ma, Ruofeng Yang, Tianzhi Ren, Kuan Yang, Shuai Li

item.title: A general reduction and explicit remoteness formulas for exact slow 2-Nim
item.description: arXiv:2611.27343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In exact slow $2$-Nim, a move removes one token from each of two nonempty piles. For any number of piles, we relate Smith remoteness in the exact game to the remoteness $D$ of Moore's slow game on the piles that remain after a largest pile is removed. If the total number of tokens $N$ is odd, the exact game has remoteness $\min(D,\lfloor N/2\rfloor)$. If $N$ is even, its remoteness equals $D$ when $2D\le N$ and is either $N/2$ or $N/2-1$ otherwise. Both values can occur for the same $N$, $D$, and number of piles. We determine $D$ explicitly for five piles. This gives a six-pile remoteness formula and a rule for selecting an optimal move. Both take $O(b)$ bit operations when each pile size has at most $b$ bits. We also give a closed formula for positions with any number of unit piles and two further piles of arbitrary size. For the GM move rule, we prove the proposed descriptions of the exceptions in the four- and five-pile games and give the exact threshold at which a specified six-pile move ceases to be optimal as the largest pile grows. Finally, we classify all outcome-preserving sorted translations for five and six piles.
item.dc:creator: Ra\'ul S\'anchez Gal\'an, Yijie Xu

item.title: A Combinatorial Construction of Symmetric Magic Squares of Order Four
item.description: arXiv:2611.27380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct all symmetric nonnegative integer matrices of order four having a common sum on every row, column, and both diagonals. The construction is a disjoint union of twelve translates of free submonoids, each with five uniquely determined nonnegative integer parameters.Twelve is the smallest possible number of classes among finite disjoint unions of translates of free submonoids generated by five elements, even when generators outside the Hilbert basis are allowed. A comparison-based case analysis supplies integer inverse formulas and assigns every point on the shared faces to exactly one class. The normal forms prove that the twelve primitive extreme-ray generators form the entire Hilbert basis: eight have magic sum two and four have magic sum four. We exhibit the underlying regular unimodular triangulation and a single perturbation direction producing all half-open boundary conventions. The resulting positive multivariate generating function specializes to an explicit rational function and a quasipolynomial of period four in the magic sum. A further consequence is a reflexive lattice polytope associated with positive symmetric magic squares.
item.dc:creator: Xinru Jiang, Yueming Zhong

item.title: Real stable multivariate Delannoy polynomials and their Rayleigh differences
item.description: arXiv:2611.27395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The univariate Delannoy polynomials are known to have only real zeros. We construct a real stable multivariate refinement of these polynomials using weighted lattice paths and give both algebraic and combinatorial proofs of stability. More strongly, we show that every Rayleigh difference of the multivariate Delannoy polynomials is a perfect square and give an explicit factorization.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen, Ruiqi Mao

item.title: Additive cubes are avoidable by a non-uniform morphism of length $6$ over $\{0,a,b\}$ (with $b \ge 4$ and $\gcd(a,b) = 1$)
item.description: arXiv:2611.27519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that additive cubes are avoidable over every ternary alphabet $\{0, a, b\}$ with $1 \le a < b$, $\gcd(a, b) = 1$, and $b \ge 4$, thereby solving and extending Rao's~(2015) conjecture from $b \ge 6$ down to $b \ge 4$. Our construction applies a single dual pair of parameterized non-uniform morphisms of image length at most~$6$ to the additive-cube-free word $\mathbf{w}$ of Cassaigne et al.~(2014). For $b \ge 10$, we prove that every additive square in the image is an abelian square, reducing additive cubes to abelian cubes; the absence of abelian cubes and the $24$ finite cases with $4 \le b \le 9$ are then certified via the finite-graph method of Jamet and Rosenfeld~(2026).
item.dc:creator: Damien Jamet

item.title: Counting cliques in optimal $1$-planar graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.27562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extremal problems concerning the maximum number of cliques in $n$-vertex graphs from a given graph class have been widely investigated. In this contribution, we present several results on counting cliques that extend beyond the existing framework. Firstly, we address this problem for the class of optimal 1-planar graphs where we determine the maximum numbers of copies of $K_3$, $K_4$, and $K_5$ in an $n$-vertex optimal 1-planar graphs and characterize all extremal graphs. This resolves Question {\b 8.1} of Gollin-Hendrey-Methuku-Tompkins-Zhang. Secondly, we prove that every 3-connected plane quadrangulation on $n\geq14$ vertices has at most $2n-14$ 3-separators and characterize the corresponding extremal graphs. This confirms Conjecture {\b 8.2} posed by Gollin-Hendrey-Methuku-Tompkins-Zhang. Lastly, we construct, for every integer $r\geq1$, a simple 2-planar graph with $5r+3$ vertices and $44r+1$ triangles, thus disproving Conjecture {\b 8.3} of theirs. Our proofs use radial graphs, tree decomposition and SPQR trees.
item.dc:creator: Shuchao Li, Liwen Lian

item.title: A proof of Cigler's quadratic recurrence for Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.27575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an integer $k\ge0$ let $a_{n,k}(x,c)$ be the generating polynomial of the Motzkin paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,k)$ that never go below height $0$, where level steps have weight $c+x$ at height $0$ and weight $c$ at positive height, and let $D_{k,n}(x,c)=\det(a_{i+j,k}(x,c))_{0\le i,j\le n-1}$. We prove that for all $k\ge0$ and $n\ge2k+2$ $$D_{k,n}D_{k,n-2k-2}-x^2D_{k,n-1}D_{k,n-2k-1}=(1-x^2)D_{k,n-k-1}^2,$$ a quadratic recurrence conjectured by J. Cigler in 2023 (eq. (18) of arXiv:2309.15557 and MathOverflow question 456683). As a by-product we obtain an expression of $D_{k,n}$ as a $k\times k$ determinant built from Chebyshev polynomials reduced modulo $U_k-xU_{k-1}$, together with a bilinear identity for these $k\times k$ determinants that holds for all integer shifts. We also give a proof of Cigler's companion conjecture that $D_{k,n}(x,c)$ equals the determinant of an explicit matrix $H_{k,n}(x)$ with entries $0$, $1$ and powers of $x$, and in particular does not depend on $c$; this statement has recently been proved by V. Jandhyala, and our proof was found independently. The proofs use Chebyshev polynomials, a model of $\mathbb{Q}(x)[X]/(U_k-xU_{k-1})$ by antisymmetric Laurent polynomials, a lemma on complementary minors, and a three-term Pl\"ucker relation.
item.dc:creator: Tianxing Yu

item.title: Determinantal upper bounds for ternary matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.27591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain a new, sharper upper bound for the determinant of a matrix of order $n \equiv 2 \pmod{3}$ with entries in the complex third-roots of unity. This bound is an analog of Ehlich's bound for binary matrices of order $n \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$ and it is obtained by first applying an appropriate normalization, or balancing, procedure for matrices with root-of-unity entries and then generalizing Ehlich's argument. This new bound achieves an asymptotic fraction of approximately 74% of the Hadamard bound.
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Munemasa, Guillermo N\'u\~nez Ponasso

item.title: The categorical graph minor conjecture and matching complexes
item.description: arXiv:2611.27657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the graph minor category $\mathcal G$ of Miyata, Proudfoot and Ramos, the morphisms are the ways of obtaining one connected graph from another by deleting and contracting edges. The categorical graph minor conjecture asserts that every submodule of a finitely generated $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{op}}$-module is finitely generated; it is known for graphs of bounded first Betti number. We disprove this conjecture: it fails for the module assigning to each graph the free module on its spanning trees, which is generated by one element. A quotient of this module has unbounded torsion. We prove, however, that the conjecture holds for all modules depending on a minor morphism only through the induced injection of edge sets. This applies to matching complexes. Let $M_d(G)$ be the complex of edge sets of $G$ spanning subgraphs of maximum degree at most $d$. We prove that the $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{op}}$-module $G\mapsto H_i(M_d(G);\mathbb Z)$ is finitely generated for all $i$ and $d$, which for $d=1$ confirms a conjecture recorded by Ramos, and that a positive integer depending only on $i$ annihilates the torsion of all these groups. The proofs combine Robertson and Seymour's labelled graph minor theorem with a new criterion: if a category has a faithful functor to finite sets and injections and, for every finite set of colours, its objects with coloured underlying sets are well-quasi-ordered by colour-preserving morphisms, then its representations over a left-Noetherian ring form a locally Noetherian category. Unlike the Gr\"obner method of Sam and Snowden, this criterion requires no ordering compatible with the morphisms.
item.dc:creator: Jiangdong Ai, Yongtang Shi

item.title: Proximity and Remoteness in Trees with given Segment Sequence
item.description: arXiv:2611.27685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The average distance of a vertex $v$ of a connected graph $G$ is the arithmetic mean of the distances from $v$ to all other vertices of $G$. The proximity $\pi(G)$ and the remoteness $\rho(G)$ of $G$ are the minimum and the maximum of the average distances of the vertices of $G$, respectively. A segment $S$ of a tree is a path-subtree whose terminal vertices are either branching or pendant vertices, and all internal vertices have degree $2$. The segment sequence $(\ell_{S_1}, \ell_{S_2},\ldots,\ell_{S_m})$ of T is the non-increasing sequence of the lengths of all segments of T. In this paper, we characterise trees with a given segment sequence that minimise proximity and those that maximise remoteness. For trees that minimise remoteness, we establish sufficient conditions under which the tree is starlike and conjecture that a remoteness-minimising tree is always either starlike or a ($\Delta,2$)-tree. For trees that maximise proximity, we derive a collection of necessary conditions that any tree maximising proximity must satisfy.
item.dc:creator: Imran Allie, Brandon Du Preez, Zion Hefty, Sonwabile Mafunda

item.title: Extremal problems for graphs with bounded $k$-th binding number
item.description: arXiv:2611.27699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The binding number of a graph, introduced by Woodall [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B, 1973], is a central topic in structural and extremal graph theory. Recently, Chen et al. introduced the $k$-th binding number $\beta^k(G)$. Anderson [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B, 1971] proved that every graph $G$ of even order with $\beta^1(G)\ge\frac43$ contains a perfect matching, and that the bound $\frac43$ is best possible. For $k\ge2$, Chen et al. proved that $\beta^k(G)\ge1$ guarantees a $k$-factor whenever $kn$ is even, and that the bound $1$ is best possible. The above facts reveal a fundamental distinction between the higher-order binding number and the classical binding number. This distinction makes extremal problems for graphs with bounded $k$-th binding number particularly intriguing. For positive integers $n,$ $k$ and $r$, we in this paper determine the maximum size and spectral radius among all graphs $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $\beta^k(G)<r$, and characterize the corresponding extremal graphs, respectively. In particular, when $k=1$, our results imply the corresponding extremal results of Fan and Lin [Electron. J. Combin., 2024] and Liu, Chen and Fan [Electron. J. Combin., 2026]. Our proofs develop a structural framework that relates higher-order neighborhood inequalities to the structure of the complements of graphs. This framework may provide an approach to Tur\'{a}n-type problem involving the $k$-th binding number, and the approach may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Ao Fan, Ruifang Liu

item.title: Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions and the Hirota-Miwa equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $k\ge0$ let $a_{n,k}(x,c)$ count Motzkin paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,k)$ that never go below height $0$, where level steps have weight $c+x$ at height $0$ and $c$ above it, and let $D_{k,n}=\det\bigl(a_{i+j,k}(x,c)\bigr)_{0\le i,j\le n-1}$. T. Yu proved Cigler's conjecture $D_{k,n}D_{k,n-2k-2}-x^2D_{k,n-1}D_{k,n-2k-1}=(1-x^2)D_{k,n-k-1}^2$ $(n\ge2k+2)$ by writing $D_{k,n}$ as a $k\times k$ determinant of Chebyshev polynomials modulo $U_k-xU_{k-1}$. Using a linear map found by Yu, we show that the recurrence is a reduction of the Hirota-Miwa equation for Casorati determinants. This gives a second proof, and the recurrence holds for $n\ge2k+2+\max(0,N-\lfloor k/2\rfloor)$ for the Hankel determinants of $n\mapsto L(X^n(U_k-xU_{k-1}))$ whenever the moment functional $L$ has the recurrence coefficients of the Chebyshev polynomials above height $N$. For any monic polynomial in place of $U_k-xU_{k-1}$ the Hirota-Miwa equation gives an identity with a free parameter between symplectic characters, and Yu's identity for rectangular characters follows from it by fixing the parameter and restricting to a line. On the curve $xc+x^2+1=0$ we express the Hankel determinants of the sequences shifted by $2$ and $-1$ through the $D_{k,n}$. There the recurrence becomes the Desnanot-Jacobi identity, which gives a third proof, and a recurrence for the Hankel determinants of odd convolution powers of Narayana polynomials, shifted backward by $k$. We also prove identities that Cigler stated as observations, an analogue of odd orthogonal type, and a factorization for paths with a weighted return step.
item.dc:creator: Haiming Sun

item.title: On the factorization of Dirac hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.27781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A celebrated result from the 70s due to Baranyai states that the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices decomposes into perfect matchings if $k\mid n$. We prove a minimum degree version of this result. Note that a necessary condition for a $k$-uniform hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices to admit a decomposition into perfect matchings is that $G$ is vertex-regular and $k\mid n$. We show that, if this is satisfied and, in addition, $G$ has minimum $(k-1)$-degree at least $(\frac{1}{2}+o(1))n$, then it indeed decomposes into perfect matchings. The constant $1/2$ is optimal, as below this threshold, $G$ might not even contain a single perfect matching. This settles a conjecture of Glock, K\"uhn and Osthus from 2021.
item.dc:creator: Yangyang Cheng, Stefan Glock, Andrew Lane

item.title: Extremal $K_t$-intersecting graph families for large $t$
item.description: arXiv:2611.27793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that for every sufficiently large positive integer $t$ and every integer $n \ge t$, every $K_t$-intersecting family $\mathcal{G}$ of graphs on vertex set $[n]$ has size at most $2^{\binom{n}{2}-\binom{t}{2}}$. Furthermore, when the equality is attained, $\mathcal{G}$ must consist of all graphs on $[n]$ that contain some fixed copy of $K_t$. Our result settles a conjecture of Ellis, Filmus, and Friedgut for sufficiently large $t$. We also present a short proof for the odd-cycle-intersecting case, slightly different from the existing proofs in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Yijia Fang, Hao Huang

item.title: Star Triangulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.27936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study full triangulations of planar point configurations consisting of $n$ points in convex position and one point in the interior, assuming that no three points are collinear (star configurations). Our main contribution is a classification of the star configurations up to combinatorial equivalence. We show that there are $2^{n-1}-n$ equivalence classes, by establishing a bijection between a star configuration and a particular Young diagram. By transforming each such Young diagram to a binary sequence, we manage to also give a combinatorial description of the orbits of these star configurations under the dihedral group action, encoding each such orbit through a black-and-white bracelet. For each star configuration, we derive an explicit formula for the number of its full triangulations, expressed in terms of Catalan numbers and the parts of the associated Young diagram. Additionally we derive a formula of these full triangulations expressed only in terms of Catalan numbers and the bead structure of the associated bracelet. Finally, we let the points move freely under the restriction that they stay in a star configuration and show that there exist $\binom{2n-3}{n-3}$ topologically distinct full triangulations.
item.dc:creator: Dimitris Bogiokas, Franziska Donhauser

item.title: Intervals of limit points for $B_{\alpha}$-spectral radii
item.description: arXiv:2611.27937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let \[ B_{\alpha}(G)=\alpha A(G)+(1-\alpha)L(G)=(1-\alpha)D(G)+(2\alpha-1)A(G),\qquad 0\leq \alpha\leq 1. \] We study the limit points of the spectral radii of these matrices. Put $a_{\alpha}=1-\alpha$, $b_{\alpha}=|2\alpha-1|$, and $w_{\alpha}=a_{\alpha}+b_{\alpha}$. We prove that, for every $\alpha\neq 1/2$ and every integer $d\geq 3$, the interval \[ \left[a_{\alpha}d+2b_{\alpha}\sqrt{d-1},\,w_{\alpha}d\right] \] consists entirely of $B_{\alpha}$-limit points. All these points are realized by connected bipartite graphs of maximum degree at most $d$. We extend the induced-subgraph interpolation of Alon and Wei from $A$ to $aD+bA$, and obtain a unified proof using bipartite Ramanujan graphs. Consecutive intervals overlap for large $d$; hence the set of $B_{\alpha}$-limit points contains a half-line for every $\alpha\neq 1/2$. At $\alpha=1/2$, one has $B_{1/2}=D/2$, and the set of spectral radii is discrete. Combining uniform edge subdivisions with generalized Bethe decorations, we improve the Laplacian and signless Laplacian half-line to $[29/5,\infty)$, verified by an exact rational certificate. We also treat two complementary tree constructions. For the starlike trees $T_{1,m,m}$, the limiting $B_{\alpha}$-spectral radius is the unique solution above the path threshold of an explicit unsquared equation. More generally, letting selected arms of a starlike tree tend to infinity produces ordered limit points with tree realizations. Finally, we give the exact affine relations among $B_{\alpha}$, the $A_{\beta}$-matrix, and the deformed Laplacian. These identify which tree and caterpillar results are reparametrizations of earlier work. The interval theorem also yields half-lines of $A_\beta$-limit points for every $0\le\beta<1$, and of deformed-Laplacian limit points for every nonzero deformation parameter.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Belardo, Callum Huntington, Elismar R. Oliveira, Vilmar Trevisan

item.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring of Cocomparability, Co-Bipartite, and Distance-Hereditary Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.26645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper vertex coloring in which every non-isolated vertex has a neighbor whose color occurs exactly once in its open neighborhood. We prove that deciding whether $\omega(G)$ colors suffice is NP-complete on connected cocomparability graphs of diameter two and independence number three. The reduction supplies a partition into three cliques, a maximum clique, an optimal ordinary coloring, and a dominating edge. Every constructed graph needs either $\omega(G)$ or $\omega(G)+1$ PCF colors. The result also gives NP-completeness on AT-free graphs. For the co-bipartite subclass, we give a complete matching characterization and an $O(n^6)$-time algorithm for an optimal coloring. The cocktail-party graphs are exactly the co-bipartite graphs requiring two more colors than their ordinary chromatic number; every other co-bipartite graph needs at most one additional color. The matching method extends to all graphs with independence number at most two, giving an $O(n^6\log n)$-time optimization algorithm. Finally, for distance-hereditary graphs, we decide whether $k$ colors suffice in $O(n+m+nk^{10})$ time and compute an optimal coloring in $O(n^{11}+m)$ time without fixing the palette size. The algorithm uses a binary decomposition and groups colors according to five possible behaviors at the boundary of a subgraph.
item.dc:creator: Gautam K. Das, Kamal Santra

item.title: Uniformising random greedy maximal independent sets on graphs with at most five vertices
item.description: arXiv:2611.26675v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A random greedy algorithm scans the vertices of a finite graph in increasing order of independent exponential arrival times and accepts each vertex unless an accepted neighbour blocks it. We ask an inverse question: can strictly positive finite arrival rates be chosen so that the terminal inclusion-maximal independent sets are all equally likely? We call this exact property exponential greedy uniformisability (EGU). We establish the complete small-order classification: every finite simple graph on at most five vertices is EGU, with the unique exception of the five-vertex path $P_5$ up to graph isomorphism. A strict $2\times2$ probability minor provides an explicit obstruction for the exceptional graph; the positive cases are certified by graph-isomorphism reduction and exact constructive witnesses. We explain the independent-exponential-clock probability law and the formal Lean 4 verification, registered as Palomar PALOMAR-2026-11-19-000021 (version 1). The registration is a formal proof record, not a claim of novelty certification or journal peer review.
item.dc:creator: John Fairfax-Ball

item.title: Littlestone Dimension and Its Dual
item.description: arXiv:2611.26721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The dual Littlestone dimension of a concept class $\mathcal{H}\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$, $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}):=\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H}^*)$, is the Littlestone dimension of the dual class $\mathcal{H}^*$, obtained by exchanging the roles of domain points and hypotheses. A classical result of Shelah implies that $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})$ and $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})$ are finite simultaneously, and quantitative results of Hodges [Mathematika, 1981] imply the doubly exponential bound $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}}$. Malliaris and Moran [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2024] asked whether this bound is optimal. We answer this by proving the improved bound \[ \operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})^2)}. \] An exponential dependence is necessary, as witnessed by the class of all binary hypotheses on a finite domain.
item.dc:creator: Pooya Hatami, Chavdar Lalov

item.title: Semi-regular admixed arrays: asymptotic enumeration and when information is additive
item.description: arXiv:2611.26990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In genomic data analysis, admixed arrays are pairs of matrices recording the local ancestry and the allele at each position of the haplotypes of admixed individuals. We study two-way diploid admixed arrays with $N$ individuals and $P$ loci under two families of constraints: local ancestry tallies, which fix the number of ancestry assignments per individual, and ancestry-specific sums, which fix the allele count per locus and ancestry. These two constraint families correspond to summaries of admixed genetic data investigated in biomedical and genomic applications. In the semi-regular regime, where all tallies and sums are uniform, we use complex martingale techniques to derive asymptotic formulas for the number of doubly constrained arrays as $N$ and $P$ grow with bounded ratio, over the whole feasible region. The leading term is governed by the Shannon entropy of the frequencies of the four possible pairs of entries at a position of the two matrices; on the boundary one or two of them vanish, changing the Gaussian correction. We then ask whether the two families carry information additively, that is, whether an independence heuristic predicts the doubly constrained count up to a bounded factor. Measured against the smallest set of arrays defined by a constraint that each family implies on its own, additivity holds only on a set of measure zero. It includes an edge of the feasible region with correction factor $e^{-1/4}$, extending our earlier result at the symmetric point. Thus, how far the two summaries jointly narrow down individual-level ancestry and genotype configurations cannot generally be predicted from how far each does on its own.
item.dc:creator: Alan J. Aw

item.title: Integral Multipliers and Arithmetic Obstructions for Two-Hidden-Layer ReLU Maxima
item.description: arXiv:2611.27018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study exact representations of maximum functions by ReLU networks with two hidden layers and integer parameters. The least positive output multiplier is two for the six-input maximum, and either two or six for the seven-input maximum. We obtain these bounds from integral cubical fillings and a coefficient-preserving passage from polytope identities to networks. For the coordinate-facet complex of the six-simplex, we compute a coning index of six over the integers and three after inverting two, allowing arbitrary integral directions within each facet. A class in the homology of the unrestricted kernel complex characterizes the remaining seven-input problem; its vanishing is equivalent to an integral filling of a fixed target. We also construct a finite character that separates rational from three-local representability in a dictionary containing two known constructions and all pairs of edge-disjoint three-edge forests. This obstruction permits nonsymmetric coefficients and is confined to the specified dictionary. Control of lower-dimensional remainders yields a sufficient criterion in the top-dimensional quotient. Exact certificates and verification programs accompany the finite calculations.
item.dc:creator: Pengcheng Cheng

item.title: The $n!$ theorem via quaternionic rotation of Cherednik algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.27113v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a proof of the $n!$ theorem based on the representation theory of Cherednik algebras and an analog of the rotation of complex structures arising from an action of the quaternions.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Griffeth

item.title: Rigidity in the Lichnerowicz inequality for word-length semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.27204v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an operator-algebraic characterization of Cayley graphs that are partial cubes, that is, embed isometrically into a hypercube. More precisely, noncommutative versions of the Lichnerowicz inequality control the spectral gap of the generator of a quantum Markov semigroup by the constant in the complete $\Gamma_2$-criterion of Junge and Zeng or the constant in the geometric Ricci criterion of Junge, LaRacuente and Li. We show that for word-length semigroups on group von Neumann algebras, equality in either of these inequalities occurs exactly when the Cayley graph is a partial cube.
item.dc:creator: Melchior Wirth

item.title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
item.description: arXiv:2611.27300v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a $3$-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code of distance exactly $2$, so the girth is not a lower bound. For a represented Lagrangian matroid and a dealer, we construct the dealer-shortened stabilizer code, its logical operators, an encoding isometry and explicit recovery maps, and we show that this is the code implemented by the stabilizer state through teleportation. A set of players recovers the secret, learns nothing, or learns part of it according to a rank formula on pairs of columns, which equals its mutual information with the dealer; for graph states it becomes a cut-rank condition. Over $\F_2$ a symplectic matroid of any rank has only one representation, so the code, its access structure and its weight enumerators depend on the matroid alone; for $q\ge3$ even the enumerator does not. Circuit-induced authorized sets always reconstruct when the matroid is self-dual, but not in general, and a six-qubit graph state shows that the two access structures can differ even then. Finally, a polynomial in the ranks of column pairs determines both weight enumerators.
item.dc:creator: Sayantan Ganguly

item.title: A Geometric Approach to the Classification of Locally-APN Niho-Type Power Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.27312v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $q=2^m$ with $m\geq 2$. We develop a geometric approach to the classification of locally-APN Niho-type power functions over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. Our approach begins with a characterization of $\mathbb{F}_q$-homogeneous functions: the conditions $D_F(a,F(a))=q$ and $D_F(a,b)\leq 2$ for every $a\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^*$ and $b\neq F(a)$ hold if and only if the projective graph of $F$ is a $(q+1)$-arc in $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$. For Niho-type power functions, this differential condition is equivalent to the locally-APN property. Applying the classification of $(q+1)$-arcs and the description of their stabilizers, we prove, for $m\geq 3$, that $F_s(x)=x^{s(q-1)+1}$ is locally-APN if and only if $s\equiv(2^k+1)^{-1}\pmod{q+1}$ for some $1\leq k\leq 2m-1$ satisfying $\gcd(k,m)=\gcd(2^k+1,q+1)=1$. Together with the known case $m=2$ and the sufficient condition of Xie et al., this gives the complete classification and confirms the conjecture of Cui, Luo, and Xiang.
item.dc:creator: Chenxu Wang, Jun Zhang

item.title: Squarefree powers of simplicial forests
item.description: arXiv:2611.27531v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The highest nonzero squarefree power of an edge ideal always has linear quotients, whereas this property can fail even for the facet ideal of a pure two-dimensional simplicial tree. This raises the question of which combinatorial conditions ensure linear quotients beyond the graph case. We characterize the squarefree powers of facet ideals of pure simplicial forests that have linear quotients, showing that this property is equivalent to having a linear resolution or being linearly related. We also investigate the corresponding question for undirected path ideals of forests. Here the highest nonzero squarefree power always has linear quotients for $3$-path ideals, whereas the analogous assertion fails for $4$-path ideals of trees.
item.dc:creator: Marie Amalore Nambi, Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, Dharm Veer

item.title: Longest run for $q$-binary trials
item.description: arXiv:2611.27828v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the longest-run distribution for binary trials in which the success probability varies geometrically. Exact formulae are derived for the probability mass function and the cumulative distribution function of the length of the longest success run in a sequence of $q$-binary trials, using enumerative combinatorics. The setting covers independent but not necessarily identically distributed zero--one trials whose success probabilities follow a geometric rule, and the classical independent and identically distributed Bernoulli longest-run distribution is recovered in the limit $q\to 1$. A simulation study confirms accurate maximum likelihood estimation of the base success probability and the geometric parameter $q$, a well-calibrated and powerful boundary-corrected likelihood ratio test of the hypothesis that $q=1$, and close agreement between the analytical cumulative distribution function and its empirical counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Jungtaek Oh, Nurzhan Sapargali

item.title: A quasi-tree expansion of the Homfly polynomial
item.description: arXiv:2611.27926v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Homfly polynomial is one of the best-studied invariants of oriented links. Here, building on work of Jaeger and others, we present a new method of computing it. Terms in the expansion are algebraically simple and they are indexed by certain quasi-trees of the Seifert graph of an (almost) arbitrary link diagram. The quasi-trees, in turn, depend on a single basepoint along the link but no more auxiliary data. This allows us to streamline the proofs of some old results and to find new ones as well, such as an upper bound on the total degree in terms of directed joins of the Seifert graph.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as K\'alm\'an, Lilla T\'othm\'er\'esz

item.title: The Power of Sampling for Finding Far-Apart Bases in Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2611.27934v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the geometry of matroids via the \emph{diameter} and \emph{dispersion} of the metric space of their bases. Given a matroid $M$, we ask if the diameter of its basis-exchange graph $\mathcal{G}(M)$ can be approximated by sampling two uniformly random bases. As our main result, we show that their expected distance is always at least $1/16$ of the diameter of $\mathcal{G}(M)$. While this might appear to follow from the edge-expansion properties established by Anari, Liu, Gharan and Vinzant (STOC'19), we show that this inutition is false by constructing a graph $G$ with edge-expansion at least $1$ for which sampling two random vertices does \emph{not} give a constant-factor approximation to its diameter. We turn to finding $k\geq 2$ maximally-diverse bases of a matroid, the $k$ (max--min) diversity problem. When $k=2$, the problem is solvable via matroid intersection. However, for $k\geq 3$ no polynomial-time approximation or hardness is known, even for diverse spanning trees. We show that sampling $k\geq 3$ bases provides a tight $\Theta(\log k)$ approximation. We then combine structural insights about the local density of $\mathcal{G}(M)$ with classical LP-rounding techniques to obtain a polynomial-time $1/6$-approximation algorithm for the $k$-diversity problem in arbitrary matroids, the first constant-factor polynomial-time approximation for max--min diversity on any matroid. A key ingredient for our result is the \emph{Farthest Matroid Basis} problem: given a collection of bases, find a new basis as far as possible from all of them. We give a polynomial-time $1/3$-approximation algorithm for this, which is our main algorithmic primitive for $k$ max--min diversity. We also show it is $W[1]$-hard when parameterized by the optimal distance. We also improve the $1/6$-approximation for $k$-diversity, for partition matroids and graphic matroids of constant arboricity.
item.dc:creator: Mayank Goswami, Vasilis Livanos, Pasin Manurangsi, Arturo Merino, GiBeom Park, Adarsh Srinivasan

item.title: Recognizing $k$-inducible Digraphs is NP-complete
item.description: arXiv:2611.27965v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A digraph is k-inducible if its arcs correspond to the pairwise majority relation of a preference profile with k voters. By McGarvey's theorem, every asymmetric digraph is k-inducible for some k, but for every fixed k there are digraphs that are not k-inducible. Whether a digraph is 1-inducible or 2-inducible can easily be decided in polynomial time. The complexity of deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible for every fixed $k\geq 3$ has been a long-standing open problem. We prove that deciding whether a tournament is 3-inducible is NP-complete and then leverage this result to show that deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible is NP-complete for every fixed $k\geq 3$. Our results imply that, unless P=NP, k-inducible digraphs cannot be characterized by finitely many forbidden induced subdigraphs.
item.dc:creator: Felix Brandt, Fabian Frank

item.title: Associativity conditions for linear quasigroups and equivalence relations on binary trees
item.description: arXiv:2310.09184v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterise the bracketing identities satisfied by linear quasigroups with the help of certain equivalence relations on binary trees that are based on the left and right depths of the leaves modulo some integers. The numbers of equivalence classes of $n$-leaf binary trees are variants of the Catalan numbers, and they form the associative spectrum (a kind of measure of non-associativity) of a quasigroup. Every group-based equivalence relation arising here can be replaced by one defined by an abelian group generated by at most two elements. The fine associative spectra form a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of rank-two subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with an additional least element. This classifies the equivalence relations completely; closed formulas for all their numbers of classes remain open.
item.dc:creator: Erkko Lehtonen, Tam\'as Waldhauser

item.title: Backbone coloring for graphs with degree 4
item.description: arXiv:2409.10201v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $\lambda$-backbone coloring of a graph $G$ with backbone $H$ is a proper vertex coloring in which the endpoints of every edge from $H$ are assigned colors which differ by at least $\lambda$. In this paper we prove that $BBC_\lambda(G,H)\le\lambda+5$ for every graph $G$ with maximum degree at most $4$ and every connected spanning bipartite backbone $H$, provided that $\lambda\ge3$. A suitable coloring can be found in linear time. The bound is sharp for $\lambda\ge4$, even for spanning tree backbones. The proof combines degree-list coloring with a balanced choice of vertices in an auxiliary bipartite multigraph. We also settle the previously open complexity status for graphs with maximum degree $4$ and connected bipartite backbones, proving NP-completeness even for spanning tree backbones for every fixed $\lambda\ge2$. Furthermore, we obtain an almost complete classification of the complexity of deciding whether $BBC_{\lambda}(G,H)\le k$ for graphs with maximum degree at most $4$ and matching, galaxy, Hamiltonian path, and spanning tree backbones. We also determine the effect of allowing isolated vertices in matching and galaxy backbones.
item.dc:creator: Krzysztof Michalik, Krzysztof Turowski

item.title: Generalized De Bruijn Words, Invertible Necklaces, and the Burrows-Wheeler Transform
item.description: arXiv:2502.12844v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define generalized de Bruijn words as those words having a Burrows--Wheeler transform that is a concatenation of permutations of the alphabet. We show that generalized de Bruijn words are in one-to-one correspondence with Hamiltonian cycles in the generalized de Bruijn graphs, introduced in the early 1980s in the context of network design. We prove that generalized de Bruijn words retain the asymptotically maximal factor complexity of ordinary de Bruijn words over a fixed alphabet. We then use this class to construct an infinite binary family on which the Burrows--Wheeler transform reduces this complexity from asymptotically maximal to the constant $2$. In particular, this shows that the BWT can substantially improve dictionary compressibility. When the size of the alphabet is a prime $p$, we define invertible necklaces as those whose BWT-matrix is nonsingular. We show that invertible necklaces of length $n$ correspond to normal bases of the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{p^n}$, and that they form an abelian group isomorphic to the Reutenauer group $RG_p^n$. Using known results in abstract algebra, we can establish a connection between generalized de Bruijn words and invertible necklaces. In particular, we highlight a correspondence between binary de Bruijn words of order $d+1$, binary necklaces of length $2^{d}$ having an odd number of $1$'s, invertible BWT matrices of size $2^{d}\times 2^{d}$, and normal bases of the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{2^{2^{d}}}$.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Fici, Est\'eban Gabory

item.title: On coarse tree decompositions and coarse balanced separators
item.dc:creator: Tara Abrishami, Jadwiga Czy\.zewska, Kacper Kluk, Marcin Pilipczuk, Micha{\l} Pilipczuk, Pawe{\l} Rz\k{a}\.zewski

item.title: Positionality of Dumont--Thomas numeration systems for integers
item.description: arXiv:2503.04487v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Introduced in 2001 by Lecomte and Rigo, abstract numeration systems provide a way of expressing natural numbers with words from a language $L$ accepted by a finite automaton. As it turns out, these numeration systems are not necessarily positional, i.e., we cannot always find a sequence $U=(U_i)_{i\ge 0}$ of integers such that the value of every word in the language $L$ is determined by the position of its letters and the first few values of $U$. Finding the conditions under which an abstract numeration system is positional seems difficult in general. In this paper, we thus consider this question for a particular sub-family of abstract numeration systems called Dumont--Thomas numeration systems. They are derived from substitutions and were introduced in 1989 by Dumont and Thomas. We exhibit conditions on the underlying substitution so that the corresponding Dumont--Thomas numeration is positional. We first work in the most general setting, then particularize our results to some practical cases. Finally, we link our numeration systems to existing literature, notably properties studied by R\'{e}nyi in 1957, Parry in 1960, Bertrand-Mathis in 1989, and Fabre in 1995.
item.dc:creator: Savinien Kreczman, S\'ebastien Labb\'e, Manon Stipulanti

item.title: An introduction to the symmetric group algebra
item.description: arXiv:2507.20706v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is an introduction to the group algebras of the symmetric groups, written for a quarter-long graduate course. After recalling the definition of group algebras (and monoid algebras) in general, as well as basic properties of permutations, we introduce several families of elements in the symmetric group algebras $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$ such as the Young--Jucys--Murphy elements, the (sign-)integrals and the conjugacy class sums. Then comes a chapter on group actions and representations in general, followed by the core of this text: a study of the representations of symmetric groups (i.e., of left $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$-modules), including the classical theory of Young tableaux and Young symmetrizers. We prove in detail the main facts including the characterization of irreducible representations (in characteristic $0$), the Garnir relations, the standard basis theorem, the description of duals of Specht modules, and the hook length formula, as well as a number of less known results. Finally, we describe several bases of $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$ that arise from the study of Specht modules, including the Murphy cellular bases. The methods used are elementary and computational. We aim to assume as little as possible of the base ring $\mathbf{k}$, and to use as little as possible from representation theory (nothing more advanced than Maschke and Jordan--H\"older). Over 100 exercises (without solutions) are scattered through the text.
item.dc:creator: Darij Grinberg

item.title: Parity in vector balancing and reverse Littlewood--Offord problems
item.description: arXiv:2510.05044v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the probability that the random signed sum $\xi_1 v_1 + \dotsb + \xi_n v_n$ lies within a given distance $r$ of the origin, where $v_1,\dotsc,v_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ are fixed unit vectors and $\xi_1,\dotsc,\xi_n$ are independently and uniformly distributed on $\{-1,+1\}$. We demonstrate that, for certain values of $r$, the infimum of this probability is sensitive to the parity of $n$. We prove that, for any $d\geq 3$, there is some $\varepsilon = \varepsilon(d) > 0$ such that for any $n \not\equiv d \mod 2$ and unit vectors $v_1,\dotsc,v_n\in \mathbb{R}^d$, there are signs $\eta_1,\dotsc,\eta_n \in \{-1,+1\}$ such that $\|\sum_{i=1}^n \eta_i v_i\| \leq \sqrt{d - \varepsilon}$. In other words, $\mathbb{P}(\| \xi_1 v_1 + \dotsb + \xi_n v_n \| \leq \sqrt{d-\varepsilon}) > 0$. This is in contrast to the case of $n\equiv d \mod 2$, in which this probability can be zero. In the case of $d=2$ and odd $n$, we give a construction demonstrating that $\mathbb{P}(\|\xi_1 v_1 + \dotsb + \xi_n v_n\| \leq 1)$ can decay exponentially as $n$ increases, improving on the previous best-known bound of $O(n^{-3/2})$.
item.dc:creator: Lawrence Hollom, Gregory B. Sorkin

item.title: Attractors of sequences coding $\beta$-integers
item.description: arXiv:2511.00650v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we describe minimal string attractors of prefixes of simple Parry sequences. These sequences form a coding of distances between consecutive $\beta$-integers in numeration systems with a real base $\beta$. Simple Parry sequences have been recently studied from this point of view and attractors of prefixes have been described. However, the authors themselves had doubts about their minimality and conjectured that attractors of alphabet size should be sufficient. We confirm their conjecture. Moreover, we provide minimal attractors of prefixes of some particular form of binary non-simple Parry sequences.
item.dc:creator: Lubom\'ira Dvo\v{r}\'akov\'a, Martina Moravcov\'a

item.title: Chromatic numbers from edge ideals: Graph classes with vanishing syzygies are polynomially $\chi$-bounded
item.description: arXiv:2512.21800v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The chromatic number $\chi$ of a graph is bounded from below by its clique number $\omega,$ but the gap between these two values can be arbitrary large. Perfect graphs are defined by the condition that $\chi=\omega$ for all induced subgraphs. An interesting relaxation are $\chi$-bounded graph classes, where $\chi\leq f(\omega)$ for some suitable function $f.$ It is not always possible to achieve this with a polynomial $f.$ The edge ideal $I_G$ of a graph $G$ is generated by monomials $x_ux_v$ for each edge $uv$ of $G.$ The bi-graded betti numbers $\beta_{i,j}(I)$ are central algebraic geometric invariants. We study the graph classes where for some fixed $i,j$ that syzygy vanishes, that is, $\beta_{i,j}(I_G)=0.$ We prove that $\chi\leq f(\omega),$ where $f$ is a polynomial of degree $2j-2i-4.$ For the elementary special case $\beta_{i,2i+2}(I_G)=0,$ this amounts to that $(i+1)K_2$--free graphs are ${\omega-1+2i \choose 2i}$--colorable, improving on an old combinatorial result by Wagon. We also show that triangle-free graphs with $\beta_{i,j}(I_G)=0$ are $(j-1)$--colorable. Complexity wise, we show that these colorings can be derived in time $O(n^3)$ for graphs on $n$ vertices. Moreover, we show that for almost all graphs with parabolic $i,j,$ there are better bounds on $\chi.$
item.dc:creator: Alexander Engstr\"om

item.title: On the singularity and the inverse of 3-colored digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2602.24274v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article investigates the singularity and invertibility of simple connected 3-colored digraphs, with particular emphasis on the classes of unicyclic and bicyclic digraphs. A digraph $G$ is said to be non-singular (resp. singular) if its adjacency matrix $A(G)$ is non-singular (resp. singular). The main objective of this article is to characterize the non-singular 3-colored unicyclic and bicyclic digraphs. For a non-singular digraph $G$, if the diagonal entries of $A(G)^{-1}$ are all zero, then $A(G)^{-1}$ can be realized as the adjacency matrix of a weighted digraph with complex weights. We characterize all non-singular 3-colored unicyclic and bicyclic digraphs for which this condition holds. Furthermore, we investigate the invertibility of these digraphs and characterize those whose inverses are also 3-colored digraphs. In particular, our characterization of the unicyclic case extends earlier results by removing the assumption that the digraph possesses a unique perfect matching.
item.dc:creator: Md Isheteyak Zaffer

item.title: The inducibility of 6-vertex graphs
item.description: arXiv:2606.00290v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The inducibility constant $\lambda_{F}$ of a graph $F$ is the asymptotically maximum induced density of $F$ in a growing sequence of graphs. This paper systematically investigates the case when $F$ has 6 vertices (and there are 78 cases to consider up to isomorphism and complementation). We show that flag algebras can compute the sharp upper bound on $\lambda_F$ in 36 cases of which, as far as the authors know, 30 are new results. In each of the solved cases, we also prove results about the structure of large (almost) extremal graphs. In particular, we establish perfect stability in all 32 cases when the extremal construction has no quasirandom parts. We also present conjectures about the value of $\lambda_{F}$ for 12 further cases (where the upper and lower bounds are very close to each other).
item.dc:creator: Levente Bodn\'ar, Jun Gao, Jared Le\'on, Xizhi Liu, Oleg Pikhurko, Shumin Sun

item.title: Vertex-Ramsey theorems for Cartesian powers of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2608.07102v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For graphs $G,H$ and positive integers $r$ and $n$ we write $G^{\square n} \xrightarrow{r} H$ if every $r$-vertex-coloring of the Cartesian power $G^{\square n}$ of $G$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$. Since chromatic number $\chi$ of $G^{\square n}$ is the same as $\chi(G)$, there is an $r$-vertex coloring of $G^{\square n}$ for $r=\chi(G)$, such that each color class is an independent set. We prove that for $r<\chi(G)$ there is a large class of graphs $H$ such that $G^{\square n} \xrightarrow{r} H$. These graphs are so-called layered graphs in a hypercube. We also show that for some graphs $G$, such as for example odd cycles or cliques, the class of layered graphs $H$ is the only one satisfying the above Ramsey property when $\chi(G)/2 < r < \chi(G)$. In addition, we prove a more general result relating Ramsey properties of $G$ and graphs $H$ such that $G^{\square n} \xrightarrow{r} H$. One of the technical tools is a Ramsey-type statement for discrete cubes $[m]^n$ that we call the Cube Layered Lemma, which is of independent interest. One of the original motivations for studying Ramsey properties of Cartesian powers of $G$ is the fact that $G^{\square n}$ is a unit distance graph if $G$ is a unit distance graph. This provides applications in Euclidean Ramsey theory.
item.dc:creator: N\'ora Alm\'asi, Maria Axenovich, Arsenii Sagdeev

item.title: Counting Near-Spanning Matchings in Latin Squares and Steiner Triple Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.11006v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Montgomery proved that for sufficiently large $n$, every Latin square of order $n$ has a partial transversal with $n-1$ cells, and every Steiner triple system of order $n$ has a matching with $\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1$ edges, thus confirming the Ryser-Brualdi-Stein conjecture for even $n$ and the conjecture of Brouwer. We prove sharp enumerative refinements of these results: there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for sufficiently large $n$, (1) every Latin square of order $n$ has $ \left((1\pm n^{-c})\frac{n}{\mathrm {e}^2}\right)^n$ partial transversals with $n-1$ cells; (2) every Steiner triple system of order $n$ has $ \left((1\pm n^{-c})\frac{n}{2\mathrm {e}^2}\right)^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$ matchings with $\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1$ edges. The first estimate confirms predictions of Montgomery and Kelly. We also provide sharp estimates for the numbers of partial transversals and matchings of every smaller size.
item.dc:creator: Yantao Tang, Yi Zhao

item.title: Polynomial Length Cycles In Tough Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.16398v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every $n$-vertex $15$-tough graph contains a cycle of length $\Omega(n^{1/20})$.
item.dc:creator: Levi Segal, Jacques Verstraete

item.title: Nashtopes and their A-discriminants
