item.description: arXiv:2610.29889v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An $n$-player game in normal form is said to be of format $\boldsymbol{d} = (d_1, \dots, d_n)$ if the $i$-th player has $d_i$ options for $1 \le i \le n$, and is said to be balanced if $d_n - 1 \le \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(d_i - 1)$. The Nash equilibria of the game correspond to solutions of the system of indifference equations for the game, with payoff differences as coefficients and strategy probabilities as variables. As such, the mixed discriminant of this system gives some information about which games could have an unusual number of totally mixed Nash equilibria. This mixed discriminant can be regarded as an $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for some matrix $\mathcal{A}$ in the sense of [Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky 1994], and the convex hull of the columns of $\mathcal{A}$ is a polytope, which we call the Nashtope. We study this $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for each balanced game format with at least three players. This discriminant is a subset of the Nash discriminant variety introduced in [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026]. We compute the codimension and degree of this discriminant for all balanced game formats, including on-boundary formats, using the Euler obstruction formula in [Matsui--Takeuchi 2011]. Our $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant locus corresponds to a special multigraded Hurwitz locus studied in [Pratt--Sodomaco--Sturmfels 2026]. As a consequence of [Pokidkin 2026], we obtain the codimensions and degrees of the irreducible components of the Nash discriminant variety for each balanced game format with at least three players, fully resolving Problem 3.8 of [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026].
item.dc:creator: Elke Neuhaus, Irem Portakal, Luca Sodomaco, Katherine Tung

item.title: The Maximum Second Zagreb Spectral Radius of Trees, Unicyclic Graphs and Bicyclic Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.05057v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The second Zagreb matrix of a graph $G$ is $Z(G)=D(G)A(G)D(G)$, where $D(G)$ and $A(G)$ are the degree matrix and the adjacency matrix of $G$. For many degree-based weighted adjacency matrices, the trees, unicyclic graphs and bicyclic graphs with the largest spectral radius have a vertex adjacent to all others, and Mei et al. conjectured this for every such matrix on unicyclic graphs. Jiang et al. showed that $Z(G)$ is a counterexample. We prove that, for $q\in\{0,1,2\}$ and every $n\ge4$, the connected graph of order $n$ and cyclomatic number $q$ maximizing the spectral radius of $Z(G)$ is unique, and is obtained from two adjacent vertices with $q$ common neighbours by attaching $n-q-2$ pendent vertices to them as evenly as possible. The only exceptions are the star for $q=0$ and $n\le7$, and the triangle with one pendent vertex at each vertex for $q=1$ and $n=6$. This confirms a conjecture of Jiang et al.\ and all three parts of a conjecture of Shen and Shan for this matrix, with best possible thresholds on $n$. For $n\ge8$, the maximum value is $\lfloor (n+q)^2/4\rfloor+(n+q)/2+7q-2+O(1/n)$, whereas the star gives only $(n-1)^{3/2}$. A key tool is a determinant criterion that reduces spectral comparisons to sign conditions on explicit polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Juan Wang, Tony Newton, Genjie Wang

item.title: Incidence Geometry with Polarity and Tiled Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.16862v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2023, Fomin and Pylyavskyy introduced the master theorem to find and prove linear incidence theorems using quadrilateral tilings of oriented surfaces. Each face of the surface corresponds to an incidence condition, which they call a coherence condition. We extend their master theorem by incorporating polarity into coherence and allowing nonorientable surfaces. Our new coherence condition can be interpreted as perpendicularity from the perspective of Cayley--Klein geometry. Moreover, a polarity incidence theorem on a nonorientable tiled surface gives rise to a self-polar linear incidence theorem on the orientation double cover. We also extend the master theorem to Hermitian polarities over division rings, with its validity depending on the topology of the surface. Finally, we determine which incidence presentations admit proofs using tilings. When such proofs exist, we express the minimum Euler genus of the corresponding tiling in terms of the fundamental group.
item.dc:creator: Yuanqi Jiang, Peixuan Liu, Zhiyuan Liu

item.title: Circuit spectra for binary matroids
item.description: arXiv:2611.23730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The circuit spectrum of a matroid is defined to be the set of circuit sizes. The circuit $e$-spectrum of a matroid is the set of circuit sizes of the matroid containing the element $e$. The circuit spectrum problem is an important problem. Erd\H{o}s (1992) conjectured that every connected graph $G$ with girth $g$ and average degree $d$ has a cycle spectrum of size at least $\Omega(d^{\lfloor (g-1)/2 \rfloor})$. Sudakov and Verstra\"{e}te (2008) proved the full conjecture of Erd\H{o}s in a stronger form. It is natural to consider the size of the circuit spectra of binary matroids. Murty (1971) characterized all connected binary matroids with circuit spectra of size one. Lemos et al. (2011) characterized the connected binary matroids with circuit spectra of size two, where the largest size is odd. For general binary matroids, it is still an open question to find a lower bound for the size of the circuit spectra. In this paper, we give best-possible such lower bounds for connected binary matroids that do not contain both the Fano matroid and its dual as minors. Let $M$ be a simple connected binary matroid that does not have both the Fano matroid and its dual as a minor, and $d\geq 3$ be the minimum cocircuit size of $M$. We prove that (1) for each element $e$ of $M$, the circuit $e$-spectrum of $M$ must have size at least $d-2$. This bound is best possible. (2) The circuit spectrum of $M$ must have size at least $d-1$, unless $M\cong F_7,F_7^*,R_{10}$. In exceptional cases, the spectrum of $M$ has size equal to $d-2$.
item.dc:creator: Bing Wei, Haidong Wu, Shunzhe Zhang

item.title: Asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares
item.description: arXiv:2611.24564v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce some new general techniques for studying asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares. Using these techniques, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the probability that a given 'small' partial Latin square $H$ is present in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (as conjectured by Divoux-Kelly-Kennedy-Sidhu). As applications, we determine which configurations are likely to appear in random Latin squares (resolving a conjecture of Allsop-Morris), we determine the asymptotic distribution of the number of $3\times 3$ Latin subsquares in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (resolving conjectures of McKay-Wanless and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney), and we show that the first two rows of a random $n\times n$ Latin square are statistically indistinguishable from a random derangement (answering a conjecture of Cameron and Cavenagh-Greenhill-Wanless).
item.dc:creator: Lenka Kopfov\'a, Matthew Kwan, Richard Montgomery, Kalina Petrova

item.title: Max-Cut on Token Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.25153v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with a positive weight assigned to each edge. A cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into two sets $X$ and $Y$; the weight of $(X,Y)$ is the sum of the weight of the edges of $G$ with one endpoint in $X$ and the other endpoint in $Y$. The Max-Cut problem asks for the maximum weight, $m(G)$, of a cut of $G$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, is the graph, $F_k(G)$, whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of vertices of $G$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. The phase-reconstruction problem for Heisenberg antiferromagnets in physics can be rephrased as a Max-Cut problem on token graphs. Motivated by this, we study the Max-Cut problem on token graphs, mainly when all edges are assigned the same weight. Our main focus is to bound $m(F_k(G))$ in terms of $m(G)$. We prove that $m(F_k(G))\geq\binom{n-2}{k-1}m(G)$, and that this bound is tight up to a multiplicative factor of $1+O(k/n)$; in the case when $k=c \cdot n$ for some constant $0 < c < 1$, we provide an example where this bound is off by a multiplicative constant factor. We also show bounds for $m(F_k(G))$ for various classes of graphs $G$. Finally, we consider the algorithmic complexity of finding $m(F_k(G))$, showing it to be NP-complete for a constant $k$, and giving evidence that, when the weights take finitely many values, it is not NP-hard for $k\geq n^{\delta}$ for any constant $\delta>0$.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Angel Alejandro-Soto, Paulo T. Araujo, Ruy Fabila-Monroy, Sergio Gerardo G\'omez-Galicia, Mohamed Hibat-Allah, Md Moshiur Rahman Raj, Mahmud Ashraf Shamim, Ana Laura Trujillo-Negrete

item.title: Rainbow Matchings in $K_{r+1}$-free Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.26280v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{G}=\{G_1,\ldots,G_s\}$ be a system of graphs on the common vertex set with $n$ vertices. A graph $F$ with $s$ edges is rainbow if there is a bijection $\phi:E(F)\to [s]$ such that $e\in E(G_{\phi(e)})$ for each $e\in E(F)$. For a family of graphs $\mathcal{F}$, the Tur\'an number $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{F})$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph which does not contain a member of $\mathcal{F}$ as a subgraph. Akiyama and Frankl proved that for $n\geq 2s$, the condition $e(G_i)>\operatorname{ex}(n,M_s)$ for each $i\in [s]$ guarantees a rainbow matching $M_s$. In this paper, we establish an analogous result for graph systems with bounded clique number. Namely, for positive integers $n,r,m$ with $n\geq 2m+2$ and $n$ sufficiently large in terms of $r$, we prove that if $G_i$ is $K_{r+1}$-free and $e(G_i)>\operatorname{ex}(n,\{K_{r+1},M_{m+1}\})$ for each $i\in [m+1]$, then $\{G_1,\ldots,G_{m+1}\}$ admits a rainbow matching $M_{m+1}$. This result can be viewed as a rainbow analogue of a theorem of Alon and Frankl on the maximum number of edges in graphs with bounded clique number and matching number for sufficiently large $n$.
item.dc:creator: Hongliang Lu, Xinxin Ma, Xing Peng

item.title: Unitarizability of weight modules over noncommutative Kleinian fiber products
item.description: arXiv:1702.08168v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Noncommutative Kleinian fiber products $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ are $\ast$-algebras attached to $(m,n)$-periodic higher spin six-vertex configurations $\mathscr{L}$. Examples include quotients of the enveloping algebra of the affine Lie algebra $A_1^{(1)}$ and of a finite W-algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_4$. We determine which simple integral weight $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$-modules carry an invariant inner product and which of them are unitarizable, and we compute the signature of the form. All three answers are read off from the vertex configuration: the signature of a module is a count of faces in a two-coloring of an eight-vertex configuration canonically attached to $\mathscr{L}$. The main tool is a one-parameter family $\Delta_\xi$ of representations of $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ by difference operators on sections of a line bundle over the face lattice. These representations carry an explicit indefinite invariant inner product, and together they contain every simple integral weight module. Along the way we show that the Casimir element of $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ is unitary.
item.dc:creator: Jonas T. Hartwig

item.title: Sharp relations between volume growth, isoperimetry and escape probability in vertex-transitive graphs
item.description: arXiv:2001.01467v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove sharp bounds on the probability that the simple random walk on a vertex-transitive graph escapes the ball of radius $r$ before returning to its starting point. In particular, this shows that if the ball of radius $r$ has size slightly greater than quadratic in $r$ then this probability is bounded from below. On the other hand, we show that if the ball of radius $r$ has volume slightly less than cubic in $r$ then this probability decays logarithmically for all larger balls. These results represent a finitary refinement of Varopoulos's theorem that a random walk on a vertex-transitive graph is recurrent if and only if the graph has at most quadratic volume growth. They also imply the existence of a gap at $0$ for escape probabilities: there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that the random walk on an arbitrary vertex-transitive graph is either recurrent or has a probability of at least $c$ of escaping to infinity. We also prove versions of these results for finite graphs, in particular confirming and strengthening a conjecture of Benjamini and Kozma from 2002. Amongst other things, we also generalise our results to give a sharp finitary version of the characterisation of $p$-parabolic vertex-transitive graphs, prove a number of sharp isoperimetric inequalities for vertex-transitive graphs, and prove a locality result for the escape probability of the random walk on a vertex-transitive graph that can be seen as an analogue of Schramm's locality conjecture for the critical percolation probability.
item.dc:creator: Romain Tessera, Matthew Tointon

item.title: Characterisation of Markov property on planar maps
item.description: arXiv:2505.05447v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We revisit, in a self contained way, the Markov property on planar maps and decorated planar maps from three perspectives. First, we characterize the laws on these planar maps that satisfy both the Markov property and rerooting invariance, showing that they are Boltzmann-type maps. Second, we provide a comprehensive characterization of random submaps, that we call stopping maps, satisfying the Markov property, demonstrating that they are not restricted to those obtained through a peeling procedure. Third, we introduce decorated metric planar maps in which edges are replaced by copies of random length intervals $[0,w_e]$, and the decorations are given by continuous functions on the edges. We define a probability measure on them that is the analogue of the Boltzmann map and show that it satisfies the Markov property even for sets that halt exploration mid-edge.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Araya, Luis Fredes, Avelio Sep\'ulveda

item.title: An exceptional set of uniformly spread Kakutani tilings of the line
item.description: arXiv:2512.23079v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $\alpha$-Kakutani substitution rule splits the unit interval into two subintervals of lengths alpha and $1 - \alpha$, for a fixed $\alpha \in (0,1)$. A simple inflation-substitution procedure produces tilings of the real line and their associated Delone sets. We show that there are precisely five distinct values of $\min(\alpha, 1 - \alpha)$ for which these sets are uniformly spread, meaning that they are a bounded displacement of a lattice. The proof of this surprising fact combines the construction and analysis of a related family of primitive substitution tilings, Solomon's criterion for uniform spreadness, and a classification of Pisot-Vijayaraghavan polynomials.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Yotam Smilansky. An exceptional set of uniformly spread Kakutani tilings of the line. Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems 61 (2027), p. 105565
item.dc:creator: Yotam Smilansky

item.title: Euler characters for general linear Lie superalgebra
item.description: arXiv:2607.01782v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: M. Gorelik and Th. Heidersdors in the papers \cite{GH} investigated Euler characters for Lie superalgebra $\frak{gl}(m,n)$ and $\frak{osp}(m.2n)$. In the present paper we also investigate Euler characters for Lie superalgebra $\frak{gl}(m,n)$ but we use a different approach and our results are formulated in different terms.
item.dc:creator: A. N. Sergeev

item.title: On the Group Randomness of 0-1 Real Sequences from Binary Linear Codes
item.description: arXiv:2607.05418v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the group randomness of 0-1 real sequences derived from a binary linear code through the spectral anlysis of a suitable normalization of the Gram matrix of a $p \times n$ random matrix whose rows are uniformly and independently drawn from those 0-1 real sequences, where $p/n \to y \in (0,1)$. We show that as $n \to \infty$, its empirical spectral distribution converges to the Marchenko-Pastur law at a rate at least of the order $n^{-1/4}$ with high probability as a consequence of eigenvalue interlacing with the $\pm 1$ sequence model studied in 2021 [14], and that its largest eigenvalue, after centering by $p+1+y$, converges to a Gaussian random variable with mean 0 and variance $4y$, provided that the dual distance of the code is at least 5. Furthermore, we show that when this is the only control parameter, the lower bound 5 is optimal in general by demonstrating that the binary Simplex codes and first-order Reed-Muller codes of dual distance 3 and 4 respectively do not possess either property.
item.dc:creator: Chin Hei Chan

item.title: Matroid Contention Resolution with Concentration
item.description: arXiv:2607.09268v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Contention resolution schemes (CRS) are widely used for rounding fractional solutions subject to combinatorial constraints. Their guarantees are typically in expectation. Such guarantees alone do not ensure that covering constraints hold, limiting the applicability to problems with covering requirements. We prove lower-tail concentration bounds for the random-order CRS of Adamczyk and W{\l}odarczyk (AW) under the intersection of $k$ matroid constraints. For every linear function with coefficients in $[0,1]$,the output attains nearly the fractional value divided by $k+1$ with failure probability exponentially small in this benchmark,independently of the ground-set size. We extend this bound to normalized monotone submodular functions: the fractional value is given by the multilinear extension, and the concentration bound accounts for the largest singleton value. These guarantees apply to both objectives and covering requirements. Our analysis bounds the fractional value lost in each update and applies a general gain--loss concentration theorem whose bounds are independent of the number of updates. We apply these bounds to obtain new approximation guarantees for matroid intersection coloring and for monotone submodular maximization under matroid, packing, and covering constraints.
item.dc:creator: Marek Adamczyk, Stephen Arndt, Benjamin Moseley, Kirk Pruhs, Michael Zlatin

item.title: Set-defined graph classes: $\chi$-boundedness meets tropical algebra
item.description: arXiv:2607.23754v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study set-defined graph classes: hereditary classes whose vertices are assigned fixed-length numerical tuples, with adjacency determined solely by equality patterns among coordinates. These classes arise in structural graph theory, communication complexity, logic, and adjacency labeling schemes. We ask when they are $\chi$-bounded, that is, when chromatic number is bounded in terms of clique number throughout the class. First, we prove a decomposition theorem: every graph in a set-defined class can be partitioned into a number of parts polynomially bounded in its clique number, each inducing a union of a bounded number of shift-colorable graphs, that is, graphs admitting a homomorphism to a shift graph. Thus bounded unions of shift-colorable graphs form the fundamental obstruction to $\chi$-boundedness in set-defined classes. For full set-defined classes, consisting of all graphs realizable by a fixed Boolean rule on equality patterns, we prove a stronger dichotomy: every such class is either polynomially $\chi$-bounded or contains the class of $D$-dimensional shift graphs for some $D \geq 2$. Moreover, we provide an algorithm that, given a Boolean-function description of a full set-defined class, decides $\chi$-boundedness of the class. It reduces the problem to feasibility of tropical linear programs, and its correctness follows from a duality with winning strategies in mean-payoff games. Conversely, every integer system of tropical inequalities, and hence every mean-payoff game, can be encoded in strongly polynomial time as a set-defined class whose non-$\chi$-boundedness is equivalent to feasibility. This provides a graph-theoretic counterpart of tropical feasibility and mean-payoff-game solvability, linking structural graph theory, tropical algebra, and game-theoretic algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Sarosh Adenwalla, Samuel Braunfeld, Tom\'a\v{s} Hons, John Sylvester, Viktor Zamaraev

item.title: Equilibrium Numbers in Non-Square Bimatrix Games
item.description: arXiv:2609.24878v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Bimatrix games may have an exponential number of mixed Nash equilibria if both dimensions of the game are allowed to grow. Bounds on their maximal number give structural insights that have been used to construct hard-to-solve games. We show new sharp or asymptotically sharp bounds on the (polynomial) number of equilibria for generic games where one dimension of the game is fixed and the number of strategies of the other player grows. These results go beyond the hitherto studied square games. Our methods employ combinatorial properties of polytopes, and recent obstructions that relate to the graph of those polytopes. For $n\ge5$, we construct $3\times n$ games that have all $2n+1$ vertices of the best-response polytope as equilibrium strategies, proved using a simple case of the 4-color theorem for planar graphs. Generic $4\times 5$ games are shown to have at most 17 equilibria, using computer calculations with existing datasets for all combinatorial types of the relevant polytopes. For $d\times n$ games, we construct games where all but a fraction of $O(1/n)$ of the maximum number of vertices are equilibrium strategies.
item.dc:creator: Constantin Ickstadt, Thorsten Theobald, Bernhard von Stengel

item.title: New best-known coverings, packing-coverings and quantizers in low dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.30513v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct periodic point sets that improve the best known covering densities in dimensions six and seven, packing-covering constants in dimensions five, six, and seven, and normalized second moments in dimensions five and six. In dimension five, a set of the original family of Cohn-Kumar-Sch\"urmann has packing-covering constant $9/\sqrt{40}$, strictly below the proven optimum for the lattice case. All seven point sets belong to a two-parameter subfamily of a four-parameter generalization of the Cohn-Kumar-Sch\"urmann family.
item.dc:creator: Sven Ahrend, Mathieu Dutour Sikiri\'c

item.title: On C*-nuclearity of graph operator systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.01676v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We classify the set of finite simple undirected graphs whose corresponding graph operator system is C*-nuclear. We prove that the operator system associated to the graph is C*-nuclear if and only if the graph is 2-chordal, as defined by McCullough. In particular, we present the first known example of a non-chordal graph whose graph operator system is C*-nuclear, as well as the first known examples of graph operator systems which are not C*-nuclear.
item.dc:creator: Adam Dor-On, Travis Russell

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37423v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the sharp bound $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$ for the threefold additive energy of every lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, with an absolute constant. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ estimate for eigenfunctions on $\mathbb{T}^2$, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical uniform $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and confirms Bourgain's conjecture in this range. For all $k\ge4$, we obtain the fixed power saving for the $k$-fold additive energy $J_k(P_n)\le C|P_n|^{2k-3-\delta}$, with absolute constants $C,\delta>0$. Applications include mean-square convergence of observables and the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang-Baxter equation arising from posets
item.description: arXiv:2611.15540v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Victoria Lebed observed that the map $(x, \, y) \mapsto (\min\{x, \, y\}, \, \max\{x, \, y\})$ on a totally ordered set is an idempotent solution of the braid equation. We extend this example in several directions, by constructing four families of solutions of the braid equation associated to posets. First, for a given poset $P$, the map $R_P$ which sorts the comparable pairs and fixes the incomparable ones is an idempotent solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is the automorphism group of the poset $P$. Combined with the classical theorem of Birkhoff, this shows that every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of an idempotent solution of the braid equation of the form $(P, \, R_P)$, for some poset $P$. Moreover, $R_P \cong R_Q$ if and only if $P \cong Q$, and the solutions of the form $R_P$ are exactly the idempotent solutions of the braid equation which permute the components of each pair. Secondly, we classify all the solutions $R$ of the braid equation on an arbitrary set $X$ such that $R(x, \, y) \in \{(x, \, y), \, (y, \, x)\}$ for all $x$, $y\in X$: they are exactly the solutions $R_{\mathcal{P}}$ associated to the decompositions $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ into posets. Finally, we associate to any finite poset $P$ two involutive solutions $D_P$ and $E_P$ of the braid equation, whose automorphism groups are $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^P \rtimes {\rm Aut} (P)$ and, if $P$ is connected and has at least two elements, the group of automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of $P$.
item.dc:creator: Gigel Militaru

item.title: Quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for Lagrangian Grassmannian
item.description: arXiv:2611.21654v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a quantum $K$-theoretic analogue of the Whitney relation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. As a consequence, we give a presentation of the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. The strategy for obtaining such relations is to use the quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for the full-flag manifold in type $C$ established by the author and Kato's pushforward map from the quantum $K$-ring of the full-flag manifold to that of the partial flag manifold. Then the Nakayama-type argument established by Gu et al., together with the classical Whitney presentation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian, gives a proof of such a presentation.
item.dc:creator: Takafumi Kouno

item.title: The Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue conjecture fails over the reals
item.description: arXiv:2611.23269v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In 1986 Bapat and Sunder asked whether $\operatorname{per}(A)$ is the largest eigenvalue of $F_A=[a_{i,j}\operatorname{per}(A(i,j))]$ for every positive semidefinite Hermitian $A$, where $A(i,j)$ deletes row $i$ and column $j$. Drury disproved this over the complex field in 2018 and conjectured that the property holds for real positive semidefinite matrices. We disprove Drury's conjecture with a rank-$4$, $32\times32$ integer Gram matrix and an integer vector whose Rayleigh quotient exceeds $\operatorname{per}(A)$; verification uses integer arithmetic. Together, the two counterexamples resolve the Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue conjecture negatively over both fields. Counterexamples exist of every order $n\ge32$. As an application to quantum optics, the violation yields a $36$-mode orthogonal interferometer and a direction of relative arrival-time delays among $32$ photons with identical-variance Gaussian wave packets along which every sufficiently small nonzero delay increases the probability that all photons are detected within four designated output modes.
item.dc:creator: Logan R. Chalmers
